items.title: GPT-5 answered 76% of past finance questions correctly.
items.summary:
GPT-5 answered 76% of past finance questions correctly.

It claimed to know only 38% of them.

This discrepancy is a problem for anyone testing AI on historical market data.

Researchers at The Fin AI created a benchmark to measure this, called FinDendro:
→ 2,226 historical US facts from 1999 to 2026
→ Monthly economic data, end-of-month stock prices, Fed decisions
→ Set up so that random guessing yields a score of about 27%

Results:
→ GPT-5 still correctly answered 61% of the facts it said it didn't know
→ It claimed to know facts up to 7 quarters ago, where its measured knowledge actually ended
→ When the model was told to "answer as of [past date]," it stopped claiming most of what it knew. Its accuracy remained the same.

My take: The model's answer to "Did you know this?" is a poor guide to what it remembers.

This doesn't mean LLMs are bad at forecasting. Backtests aren't reliable for any period the model has already seen.

What this means for you:
If someone shows you an AI that "predicted" the market in 2023, ask one question first: Was 2023 in its training data?

The stated knowledge cutoff won't determine this. Neither will the model's own answer.

Link👇

items.title: Going beyond frontier capabilities
items.summary:
Going beyond frontier capabilities

Last week, for the first time, we got a step ahead of the AI frontier.

We gave Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1-Sol and GPT-6-Astra the same 12 long-horizon RL tasks and asked them to find the holes.

Our pipeline caught four flaws in AI training tasks that none of them fully caught. Sol and Astra missed 5 more on top of that. 

Three of the four actually sit in security-sensitive code, which is honestly pretty worrying. Train a model on tasks like these and it learns that lax security patterns get rewarded.

How we got here: every flaw our team finds by hand teaches our system what to look for next time. We’ve spent the last few months going deep on exactly one thing, finding what’s broken in AI training data, and it’s starting to compound.

That’s why this matters. Train on a flawed task and you’re paying to teach a model to reward hack. Models are already doing it on their own: just in September, OpenAI reported one of its own agents reward hacking a benchmark to get the answer key.

And if the best public models can’t spot flaws like these, they can’t be relied on to check their own training data either. We believe the same flywheel works anywhere models learn from structured data, and we’ve started talking with robotics and financial data companies about it. Longer term, we want to be for AI training tasks what PSA is for trading cards: a stamp of quality that people trust, backed by an index built on public data (we’re already building this!).

We’re honestly really excited to see where this goes. If you build RL tasks or training data and want to know what’s hiding in it, send us one and we’ll take a look. Looking a little past the horizon is kind of the whole point.

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips | TechCrunch
items.summary:
The chip launch comes as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and even AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are working on their own lines of AI-specific semiconductors and accompanying software in order to reduce their reliance on the dominance of Nvidia.

The news also comes at a particularly vulnerable moment for Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend admitted to having an affair with someone alleged to be a Chinese spy. [...] Meanwhile, TPU 8i Max basically combines two of the inference-focused TPU 8i chips the company launched in April, doubling the memory capacity, processing power and bandwidth, but in a single package. The result is a chip that lets AI models handle a larger range of information during queries. [...] TPU 8tx, designed with AMD, is based on the TPU 8t chip, and is geared specifically for confidentially training and running AI models, Google said in a blog post. The chip “builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use,” the company wrote.

# AI for a planet under pressure

## Editors: Victor Galaz & Maria Schewenius

## Artificial intelligence (AI) is already driving scientific breakthroughs in a variety of research fields, ranging from the life sciences to mathematics. This raises a critical question: can AI be applied both responsibly and effectively to address complex and interconnected sustainability challenges? [...] This report explores the potential and limitations of using AI as a research method in eight issue areas: Preparing for a Future of Interconnected Shocks, Understanding a Complex Earth System, Stewarding Our Blue Planet, Securing Freshwater for All, Enhancing Nature’s Contributions to People, Prospering on an Urban Planet, Improving Sustainability Science Communication, and Collective Decisions for a Planet Under Pressure.

items.title: OpenAI’s Plan to Stop AI Data Centres Overloading the Grid | Energy Digital
items.summary:
A vocal section of the American electorate were seeking assurances that AI companies will not overload power grids, while many candidates ran on a ticket of holding hyperscalers to account.

Before a single vote was counted, though, OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, had unveiled its ‘Grid Protectors Program’ – an initiative that will see its future computing campuses ease pressure on the grid. [...] “Data centres are paying more so families and small businesses can pay less, and our goal with every contract we sign under this framework is to deliver value for them,” she says

At OpenAI, the bigger picture is always in focus.

“With US data centre capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030⁠, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most,” the company says. [...] OpenAI is working to ensure its data centres can actually benefit grids, rather than overloading them. Credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty

## What is OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program?

The programme, which was announced on 2 November, commits the company to working with utilities, regulators and policymakers on arrangements for cutting the power use of its data centres at times of need.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary:
OpenAI needs to build analytics that show advertisers the consumer intent based on their prompts. I want to know which categories of intent my impressions ran against. I want to know whether those people were exploring, comparing, or ready to act, and which needs and product criteria drove that engagement. I want to know which kinds of sweater prompts turned into business and, just as important, which didn’t. Google’s advertisers have had some version of that map for two decades. It’s why [...] |

That comparison is where every sweater brand wants to be standing, and OpenAI has started selling the spot. Advertisers can buy on a CPM or CPC basis through OpenAI’s beta self-service Ads Manager, measure conversions with a pixel and Conversions API, and access campaign-level performance reporting. OpenAI is also testing Sponsored Agents, which let a user start a separate conversation with an advertiser after clicking an ad.

So the plumbing exists.

## A SEARCH-CALIBER AD PLATFORM [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.

items.title: SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI: 3 giant IPOs and only 1 has sold shares
items.summary:
OpenAI has little reason to hurry while private investors keep funding it, and it has closed $11 billion in new money. The company has also given its own reason to wait. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company," OpenAI said in a statement, as reportedby CNBC. Public buyers would also have to judge a trillion-dollar price without some basic facts about the business. Most of OpenAI's sales come from [...] The private valuation has climbed fast, and the figure public buyers will pay is still unsettled. Private investors valued OpenAI at $852 billion in late March, according to CNBC. Sam Altman, OpenAI's chief executive, is aiming for a $1 trillion valuation in the listing, according to Bloomberg reporting carried by The Next Web. That target is lower than what private investors last paid, which means the debut may not be priced at the private peak. Whether public buyers match the latest round or [...] The verdict on Anthropic will come only after trading begins, when buyers without a business stake decide whether $78 a share was worth paying.

## OpenAI

Illustration: Quartz

OpenAI has not yet sold a single share to the public, but private investors already value it at $1.25 trillion, according to Reuters. That valuation puts its planned listing among the largest stock market debuts. Nobody yet knows how much stock OpenAI will sell or when, so the size of its debut remains unknown.
